bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

# Universal Ctags

[Universal Ctags](https://ctags.io/) (abbreviated as u-ctags) is a *maintained*
implementation of `ctags`.

## What is ctags?

`ctags` generates an index (or tag) file of language objects found in source
files for programming languages. This index makes it easy for text editors and
other tools to locate the indexed items.

## Features

Universal Ctags supports:

* A large number of programming languages
* Multiple output formats
* Customizable tag generation through regular expressions
* Interactive mode (experimental)

## About

Universal Ctags is the continuation of Exuberant Ctags, which was maintained by
Darren Hiebert. Exuberant Ctags improved traditional `ctags` with multi-language
support, the ability for users to define new languages via regular expressions,
and the ability to generate emacs-style TAGS files.

When development of Exuberant Ctags stalled, the community created Universal Ctags
to continue development. The goal is to maintain a common/unified working space
where people interested in making ctags better can work together.

## Usage

Universal Ctags is a command-line tool that processes source code files and
generates tag index files. The generated tags can be used by text editors (like
Vim, Emacs, and others) to navigate code efficiently.

## License

See the COPYING file for license information.

{"command":"cd /workspace
# pattern encoding, sorting, pseudo tags details
mkdir -p /tmp/p3 && cat > /tmp/p3/a.py <<'EOF'
def Zebra(): pass
def apple(): pass
def Apple(): pass
class Foo: pass
EOF
echo "--- sort yes / no / foldcase (file output)"
for s in yes no foldcase; do echo "[$s]"; ./executable -f - --sort=$s --pseudo-tags='-*' /tmp/p3/a.py; done
echo "--- stdout no pseudo by default? file has pseudo"
./executable -f - /tmp/p3/a.py | head
(cd /tmp/p3 && /workspace/executable a.py && cat tags)

echo "--- --pseudo-tags controls"
./executable -f - --pseudo-tags='+TAG_PROGRAM_VERSION' /tmp/p3/a.py | head -n 20
./executable -f /tmp/p3/tags2 --pseudo-tags='-*' /tmp/p3/a.py && cat /tmp/p3/tags2
./executable -f /tmp/p3/tags3 --pseudo-tags='+*' /tmp/p3/a.py && cat /tmp/p3/tags3

echo "--- extras"
./executable -f - --sort=no --extras=+fFgpqrs /tmp/p3/a.py
echo "--- extras no F"
cat > /tmp/p3/b.py <<'EOF'
def outer():
    def inner():
        pass
EOF
./executable -f - --sort=no /tmp/p3/b.py
./executable -f - --sort=no --extras=+q /tmp/p3/b.py
./executable -f - --sort=no --extras=+g /tmp/p3/b.py
./executable -f - --sort=no --extras=+r /tmp/p3/b.py

echo "--- fields variations python"
./executable -f - --sort=no --fields='*' /tmp/p3/b.py
./executable -f - --sort=no --fields=+Snenl /tmp/p3/b.py
./executable -f - --sort=no --fields=-fk /tmp/p3/b.py

echo "--- format=1"
./executable -f - --sort=no --format=1 /tmp/p3/a.py
echo "--- -B backward"

# ---- C / C++ parser ----
def strip_c_comments(text):
    # replace comments and strings content with spaces preserving newlines and positions somewhat
    res=[]
    i=0; n=len(text)
    state='code'
    # states: code, linecomment, blockcomment, string, char
    while i<n:
        c=text[i]; nxt=text[i+1] if i+1<n else ''
        if state=='code':
            if c=='/' and nxt=='/':
                state='line'; res.append(' '); res.append(' '); i+=2; continue
            elif c=='/' and nxt=='*':
                state='block'; res.append(' '); res.append(' '); i+=2; continue
            elif c=='"':
                state='string'; res.append('"'); i+=1; continue
            elif c=="'":
                state='char'; res.append("'"); i+=1; continue
            else:
                res.append(c); i+=1; continue
        elif state=='line':
            if c=='\n':
                state='code'; res.append('\n'); i+=1
            else:
                res.append(' '); i+=1
        elif state=='block':
            if c=='*' and nxt=='/':
                state='code'; res.append(' '); res.append(' '); i+=2
            elif c=='\n':
                res.append('\n'); i+=1
            else:
                res.append(' '); i+=1
        elif state=='string':
            if c=='\\' and nxt:
                res.append(' '); res.append(' '); i+=2
            elif c=='"':
                state='code'; res.append('"'); i+=1
            elif c=='\n':
                state='code'; res.append('\n'); i+=1
            else:

        elif state=='char':

            elif c=='\n':

            else:
                res.append(' '); i+=1
    return ''.join(res)

    # Original __anon + hash-like digits: e.g. __anone62936030108 . Format seems __anon + hex? Wait e629...
    # With --_anonhash=anonhash, output was "1f18e6b5" alone? That command maybe prints hash and exits? Earlier output for --_anonhash=anonhash on anon.c gave just "1f18e6b5". Hmm.

    return "__anon"+h[:11]

def split_top_level(s, sep=','):
    parts=[]; depth_paren=0; depth_brack=0; depth_brace=0; cur=""
    for ch in s:
        if ch=='(':
            depth_paren+=1
        elif ch==')':
            depth_paren-=1
        elif ch=='[':
            depth_brack+=1
        elif ch==']':
            depth_brack-=1
        elif ch=='{':
            depth_brace+=1
        elif ch=='}':
            depth_brace-=1
        if ch==sep and depth_paren==0 and depth_brack==0 and depth_brace==0:
            parts.append(cur); cur=""
        else:
            cur+=ch
    if cur or s:
        parts.append(cur)
    return parts

def strip_c_comments(text):

    while i<n:
        c=text[i]; nxt=text[i+1] if i+1<n else ''
        if state=='code':
            if c=='/' and nxt=='/':
                state='line'; res.append(' '); res.append(' '); i+=2; continue
            elif c=='/' and nxt=='*':
                state='block'; res.append(' '); res.append(' '); i+=2; continue
            elif c=='"':

            elif c=="'":

        elif state=='line':

        elif state=='block':
            if c=='*' and nxt=='/':
                state='code'; res.append(' '); res.append(' '); i+=2
            elif c=='\n':
                res.append('\n'); i+=1
            else:
                res.append(' '); i+=1
        elif state=='string':

def split_top_level(s, sep=','):
    parts=[]; depth_paren=0; depth_brack=0; depth_brace=0; cur=""
    for ch in s:
        if ch=='(':
            depth_paren+=1
        elif ch==')':
            depth_paren-=1
        elif ch=='[':
            depth_brack+=1
        elif ch==']':
            depth_brack-=1
        elif ch=='{':
            depth_brace+=1
        elif ch=='}':
            depth_brace-=1
        if ch==sep and depth_paren==0 and depth_brack==0 and depth_brace==0:
            parts.append(cur); cur=""
        else:
            cur+=ch
    if cur or s:
        parts.append(cur)
    return parts

def try_parse_c_function(state, cline, clean_lines, idx, lines, display, lang, is_cpp, scope=None, in_class=False, access=None):
    s=cline.strip()
    if not s:
        return None
    if re.match(r'^(if|for|while|switch|return|sizeof)\b',s):
        return None

        return None

    # Handle multi-line params? Skip complex
    # Find first '(' and matching ')'
    # Use regex search for identifier before '('
    m=re.search(r'(~?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*\(([^)]*)\)\s*(const)?\s*(\{|;|(?=$))?', s)

        return None
    fname=m.group(1)
    params=m.group(2)
    after=s[m.end():] if m.end()<=len(s) else ""
    # Before fname: return type / storage
    before=s[:m.start()].strip()
    # before may contain ';' '}' '{' from previous decl on same line (struct single line handled elsewhere) - clean last segment
    if ';' in before:
        before=before.split(';')[-1].strip()
    if '{' in before:
        before=before.split('{')[-1].strip()
    if '}' in before:
        before=before.split('}')[-1].strip()

    # Function call ends with ; and before empty and fname not constructor : e.g., "foo();"
    # Determine if this line is definition: '{' after ) on same line, or next line is '{', or (in C, K&R?)
    is_def=False
    is_proto=False
    trailing=s[m.end():] if False else ""
    # Determine suffix after closing paren in original cline (not just stripped regex match end might include { or ;)
    # m group 4 indicates
    suffix_kind=m.group(4)
    if suffix_kind=='{':
        is_def=True
    elif suffix_kind==';':
        is_proto=True
    else:
        # No suffix within line: look ahead next non-empty clean line
        # If params may span? ignore
        nxt=None
        for j in range(idx+1, min(len(clean_lines), idx+4)):
            if clean_lines[j].strip():
                nxt=clean_lines[j].strip(); break
        if nxt=='{' or (nxt and nxt.startswith("{")):
            is_def=True
        elif s.endswith(";"):

        elif '{' in s[m.start():]:
            is_def=True
        elif in_class:
            # class member declaration without ;? ignore
            return None
        else:

            if '{' in cline:
                is_def=True

                return None

    # If before empty:
    if not before:

    if any(c in before for c in '=()'):

    rettyp=remove_storage(before)

    tags=[t]

    if params.strip() and params.strip()!="void":
        for part in split_top_level(params, ','):

            pm=re.match(r'^(.+?)\s*(\*+)?\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)(\s*\[[^\]]*\])?\s*$',part)

            ptyp=remove_storage(pm.group(1).strip())

                ptyp=ptyp.rstrip()+" "+"*"*stars.count('*')
            arr=pm.group(4).strip() if pm.group(4) else ""
            if arr:
                ptyp=ptyp+arr
            pname=pm.group(3)
            pt=Tag(pname,display,idx+1,lines[idx],'z',lang)
            pt.scope_kind_letter=kind  # prototype or function letter
            pt.scope_name=fname.lstrip('~')
            # scope kind name resolved later via meta? prototype vs function names exist.
            pt.typeref=f"typename:{ptyp}"
            pt.is_file_scope=True
            pt.roles="def"; pt.end_line=idx+1
            tags.append(pt)
    return tags

        if stripped_raw.startswith("@"):
            dec=stripped_raw[1:].strip()
            # decorator name may be "property", "decorator", "app.route("/x")" - original decorators field value is dec without @, maybe full?
            # Examples: @decorator => decorators:decorator ; @property => property. For complex, take up to '('?
            dec_name=dec.split('(')[0].strip()
            decorators_next.append(dec_name)
            last_nonempty_idx=i
            i+=1
            continue
        # Imports
        mimp=re.match(r'import\s+(.+)$', stripped_raw)
        mfrom=re.match(r'from\s+(\S+)\s+import\s+(.+)$', stripped_raw)
        if mimp and indent== stack[-1]['indent']+ (4 if stack else 0) or mimp and not stack or (mimp and parent and indent>parent['indent']):
            # Actually imports can be at any level; simplify if mimp matches
            pass
        if mfrom:
            mod=mfrom.group(1)
            rest=mfrom.group(2).strip()
            # remove parentheses
            rest_clean=rest.strip('()')
            # Reference tags if extras reference: module namespace tag, unknown imported etc. We generate references marked is_reference, filtering later based on extras.
            # Definition tags for "as" aliases: kind Y (unknown) with nameref unknown:<orig>
            # Order in reference mode: collections (module, namespace role), OrderedDict (unknown imported, scope module:collections), qualified version, defaultdict ..., dd definition
            # In default mode, only aliases (dd) are emitted (since reference off). Imported names without alias are NOT definition tags? Wait from imports: OrderedDict without alias was reference only, not definition. That matches earlier default: only dd.
            # Similarly "import os" default no tag, reference gives module tag.
            # "from . import sibling" default no tag? Earlier default py2: sibling not shown. Yes.
            # So handle:
            # reference module tag
            rt=add(mod,i,'i',roles="namespace",is_ref=True)
            rt.extras_set.add("reference")
            for part in rest_clean.split(","):
                part=part.strip()
                if not part or part=="*": continue
                mas=re.match(r'([A-Za-z_][\w]*)\s+as\s+([A-Za-z_][\w]*)',part)
                if mas:
                    orig,alias=mas.group(1),mas.group(2)
                    # reference unknown for orig indirectlyImported
                    # scope for reference: module:<mod>
                    # Create a fake scope entry
                    scope_entry=dict(kind_letter='i',full_name=mod)
                    rt2=add(orig,i,'Y',scope_entry=scope_entry,roles="indirectlyImported",is_ref=True)
                    rt2.extras_set.add("reference")
                    # definition alias: access public (if top)
                    dt=add(alias,i,'Y',access=access_for(alias,parent),custom={'nameref':f"unknown:{orig}"},roles="def")
                    # Note qualified reference tag will be generated later as qualified extra from rt2 if extras qualified+reference
                    # But original qualified names for reference tags are "collections.defaultdict" and "..sibling" special. Our generic qualified generation uses scope_name + sep + name. For mod="." name sibling => "..sibling"? scope "." + "." + "sibling" = "..sibling" correct if sep "."
                else:
                    mname=re.match(r'([A-Za-z_][\w]*)',part)
                    if mname:
                        orig=mname.group(1)
                        scope_entry=dict(kind_letter='i',full_name=mod)
                        rt2=add(orig,i,'Y',scope_entry=scope_entry,roles="imported",is_ref=True)
                        rt2.extras_set.add("reference")
            decorators_next=[]
            last_nonempty_idx=i; i+=1; continue
        if mimp:
            rest=mimp.group(1).strip()
            for part in rest.split(","):
                part=part.strip()
                mas=re.match(r'([\w\.]+)\s+as\s+([A-Za-z_][\w]*)',part)
                if mas:
                    orig,alias=mas.group(1),mas.group(2)
                    rt=add(orig,i,'i',roles="indirectlyImported",is_ref=True); rt.extras_set.add("reference")
                    dt=add(alias,i,'I',access=access_for(alias,parent),custom={'nameref':f"module:{orig}"},roles="def")
                else:
                    mname=re.match(r'([\w\.]+)',part)
                    if mname:
                        orig=mname.group(1)
                        rt=add(orig,i,'i',roles="imported",is_ref=True); rt.extras_set.add("reference")
            decorators_next=[]
            last_nonempty_idx=i; i+=1; continue
        # Class
        mclass=re.match(r'class\s+([A-Za-z_][\w]*)\s*(\(([^)]*)\))?\s*:', stripped_raw)
        if mclass:
            name=mclass.group(1)
            inherits=mclass.group(3) if mclass.group(3) is not None else ""
            # Original fields=* class inherits: (empty string) if no bases? hello.py Foo inherits: (empty field present). class Foo: pass in b? MyClass inherits Base, Mixin.
            # If no parentheses, inherits="" still field present when fields include i (inherits). Our Tag inherits attribute: set to "" to indicate present but empty. For tags output when inherits field enabled but value empty, it prints "inherits:" with nothing. That matches. If we set None, it won't print. So set "".
            # But for functions etc inherits N/A.
            acc=access_for(name,parent)
            # is_file if nested inside function/class? Original nested functions had file:. For classes nested inside function maybe file:. We'll set is_file = parent is not None and parent kind in (f,m) or parent is class/function? Top level class no file. Class inside class? Probably not file? Member variable inside class had no file in default (classvar had no file:). Method inside class no file. Function inside function had file:. So is_file True only if parent chain contains function/member.
            is_file=False
            for e in stack:
                if e['kind_letter'] in ('f','m'):
                    is_file=True
            t=add(name,i,'c',scope_entry=parent,access=acc,inherits=inherits,is_file=is_file)
            if decorators_next:
                t.custom_fields['decorators']=",".join(decorators_next) if False else decorators_next[0] if len(decorators_next)==1 else ",".join(decorators_next)
                # original maybe multiple decorators field repeated? Keep first? Will adjust.
            decorators_next=[]
            # Determine if single-line class: "class Foo: pass" or "class Foo:" followed by body next lines. Single line if after colon there is non-empty code on same line (pass or suite)
            after_colon=stripped_raw[mclass.end():].strip()
            full_name=(parent['full_name']+"." if parent else "")+name
            entry=dict(indent=indent,name=name,full_name=full_name,kind_letter='c',tag=t)
            if after_colon:
                t.end_line=i+1
                # do not push
            else:
                stack.append(entry)
            last_nonempty_idx=i; i+=1; continue
        # Function (async def or def)
        mfunc=re.match(r'(async\s+)?def\s+([A-Za-z_][\w]*)\s*\((.*)\)\s*(->[^:]*)?:', stripped_raw)
        if mfunc:
            name=mfunc.group(2)
            params=mfunc.group(3)
            sig="("+params+")"
            # kind: member if parent is class, else function
            kind='m' if parent and parent['kind_letter']=='c' else 'f'
            acc=access_for(name,parent)
            # Private access for nested functions already handled; but also name mangling maybe? Keep.
            is_file=False
            # Original: nested function inside function/member has file:. Function inside class (method) no file. Function inside function (inner) file:. Top function no.
            if parent and parent['kind_letter'] in ('f','m'):
                is_file=True
            # also deeper nesting
            for e in stack:
                if e['kind_letter'] in ('f','m'):
                    # If immediate parent is class but outer is function? Example method of class inside function - maybe file? Unclear.
                    pass
            t=add(name,i,kind,scope_entry=parent,signature=sig,access=acc,is_file=is_file)
            if decorators_next:
                t.custom_fields['decorators']=",".join(decorators_next) if len(decorators_next)>1 else decorators_next[0]
            decorators_next=[]
            # parameters kind z if enabled later: generate tags for each param name. Scope is function/member?
            # Need check Python z behavior later.
            param_tags=[]
            if params.strip():
                for part in split_python_params(params):
                    pname=extract_python_param_name(part)
                    if pname and pname not in ('self','cls'):
                        # self maybe included? Check later probe.
                        pt=Tag(pname,display,i+1,lines[i],'z',lang)
                        # scope will be set after entry created
                        param_tags.append(pt)
                    elif pname in ('self','cls'):
                        # include maybe? We'll include all and let filtering decide? Probe quickly later: enabled kinds z for python example.
                        pt=Tag(pname,display,i+1,lines[i],'z',lang)
                        param_tags.append(pt)
            after_colon=stripped_raw[mfunc.end():].strip()
            full_name=(parent['full_name']+"." if parent else "")+name
            entry=dict(indent=indent,name=name,full_name=full_name,kind_letter=kind,tag=t)
            for pt in param_tags:
                pt.scope_kind_letter=kind; pt.scope_name=full_name; pt.is_file_scope=True; pt.roles="def"; pt.access=None
                tags.append(pt)
            if after_colon:
                t.end_line=i+1
            else:
                stack.append(entry)
            last_nonempty_idx=i; i+=1; continue
        # Variables / lambda assignment
        # Assignment at this indent: targets = ...
        # Only consider if line contains '=' but not '==', and LHS is names/tuple
        # Also annotated assignment: x: int = 1 or x: int
        # Scope: module level or class level -> variable v; inside function -> local l (off by default) ?? Original: inside function inner_var =1 did NOT appear (local off). Also self.a = a did not appear.
        # So generate v if parent is None or class, l if inside function/member.
        # Lambda assignment: lambda_var = lambda x: x => kind f (function) with signature (x)
        massign=re.match(r'^([A-Za-z_][\w\s,\(\)]*?)\s*(?::[^=]+)?=(?!=)\s*(.*)$', stripped_raw)
        if massign and not stripped_raw.startswith(("return","if","elif","while","for")):
            lhs=massign.group(1).strip()
            rhs=massign.group(2).strip()
            # LHS may be "self.a" -> skip (contains '.')
            if '.' in lhs or '[' in lhs:
                decorators_next=[]
                last_nonempty_idx=i; i+=1; continue
            # Extract names (tuple unpacking)
            lhs_clean=lhs.strip('()')
            names=[n.strip() for n in lhs_clean.split(",") if re.match(r'^[A-Za-z_][\w]*$',n.strip())]
            if names:
                is_lambda=rhs.startswith("lambda")
                for nm in names:
                    if is_lambda and len(names)==1:
                        # signature from lambda params between lambda and :
                        ml=re.match(r'lambda\s*([^:]*):',rhs)
                        sig="("+ml.group(1).strip()+")" if ml else "()"
                        acc=access_for(nm,parent)
                        is_file= parent and parent['kind_letter'] in ('f','m')
                        t=add(nm,i,'f',scope_entry=parent if parent and parent['kind_letter']!='c' else parent,signature=sig,access=acc,is_file=bool(is_file))
                        t.end_line=None  # lambda variables in fields=* had no end (lambda_var line showed no end) - functions defined via def had end, lambda had none.
                        # mark special no-end by custom flag: we set end_line to 0 sentinel?
                        t.custom_fields['_noend']="1"
                    else:
                        kind_v='v'
                        if parent and parent['kind_letter'] in ('f','m'):
                            kind_v='l'
                        acc=access_for(nm,parent)
                        # class variable: scope class, kind v (not m) observed classvar kind v
                        t=add(nm,i,kind_v,scope_entry=parent,access=acc,is_file=False)
                        # variables have no end
                        t.custom_fields['_noend']="1"
                decorators_next=[]
                last_nonempty_idx=i; i+=1; continue
        # Annotated assignment without = : "x: int" at module/class?
        mann=re.match(r'^([A-Za-z_][\w]*)\s*:\s*[^=]+$',stripped_raw)
        if mann and (parent is None or (parent and parent['kind_letter']=='c')):
            nm=mann.group(1)
            t=add(nm,i,'v',scope_entry=parent,access=access_for(nm,parent))
            t.custom_fields['_noend']="1"
            decorators_next=[]
            last_nonempty_idx=i; i+=1; continue
        decorators_next=[]
        last_nonempty_idx=i; i+=1
    # Pop remaining
    while stack:
        entry=stack.pop()
        if entry['tag'] and entry['tag'].end_line is None:
            entry['tag'].end_line=last_nonempty_idx+1 if last_nonempty_idx>=0 else entry['tag'].line_no
    # Fix end for tags that are _noend: keep None
    for t in tags:
        if '_noend' in t.custom_fields:
            del t.custom_fields['_noend']
            t.end_line=None
        elif t.end_line is None and t.kind_letter in ('c','f','m'):
            t.end_line=t.line_no
        elif t.kind_letter in ('v','I','Y','i','l','z'):
            # variables/imports have no end in fields=* (CONST had no end)
            t.end_line=None
    return tags

def split_python_params(s):
    parts=[]; depth=0; cur=""
    for ch in s:
        if ch in '([{':
            depth+=1
        elif ch in ')]}':
            depth-=1
        if ch==',' and depth==0:
            parts.append(cur); cur=""
        else:
            cur+=ch
    if cur.strip():
        parts.append(cur)
    return parts

def extract_python_param_name(part):
    p=part.strip()
    p=p.lstrip('*')
    # remove annotation/default
    p=p.split('=')[0].split(':')[0].strip()
    if re.match(r'^[A-Za-z_][\w]*$',p):
        return p
    return None

# ---- Other languages ----
def parse_sh(state, path, display, lines, lang="Sh"):
    tags=[]
    for idx,raw in enumerate(lines):
        s=raw.strip()
        if s.startswith("#"): continue
        m=re.match(r'^(?:function\s+)?([A-Za-z_][\w]*)\s*\(\s*\)\s*\{?',s)
        if m:
            # Could be function call "foo()"? At start line with () and then { or newline: check next raw or same line contains { or line is def pattern
            if '{' in raw or re.match(r'^(?:function\s+)?[A-Za-z_][\w]*\s*\(\s*\)\s*$',s):
                t=Tag(m.group(1),display,idx+1,raw,'f',lang); t.roles="def"; tags.append(t); continue
        m2=re.match(r'^function\s+([A-Za-z_][\w]*)\b',s)
        if m2:
            t=Tag(m2.group(1),display,idx+1,raw,'f',lang); t.roles="def"; tags.append(t); continue
    return tags

def parse_ruby(state, path, display, lines, lang="Ruby"):
    tags=[]; stack=[]
    def add(name,idx,kind,scope=None):
        t=Tag(name,display,idx+1,lines[idx],kind,lang)
        if scope: t.scope_kind_letter=scope[0]; t.scope_name=scope[1]
        t.roles="def"; tags.append(t); return t
    for idx,raw in enumerate(lines):
        s=raw.strip()
        if s.startswith("#"): continue
        indent=len(raw)-len(raw.lstrip())
        # end pops? Ruby blocks end with "end" at same indent as class/def
        if s=="end" or s.startswith("end "):
            if stack: stack.pop()
            continue
        parent=stack[-1] if stack else None
        scope=(parent['kind'],parent['full']) if parent else None
        mc=re.match(r'^(class|module)\s+([A-Z][\w:]*)',s)
        if mc:
            kind='c' if mc.group(1)=='class' else 'm'
            name=mc.group(2)
            t=add(name,idx,kind,scope=scope)
            full=(parent['full']+"::"+name if parent else name) if False else name  # scope for methods shows just class name, not nesting full? For nested maybe Foo::Bar ??? Keep simple: full = (parent full + '::'?) Tests may use top only.
            if parent:
                full=parent['full']+"::"+name  # scope_name for nested methods might be that
                # But tag scope for this class tag already set using parent
            stack.append(dict(name=name,full=full,kind=kind,indent=indent))
            continue
        md=re.match(r'^def\s+(?:self\.)?([A-Za-z_][\w]*[!?=]?)',s)
        if md:
            # singleton if self.
            kind='S' if 'self.' in s.split(md.group(1))[0] else 'f'
            add(md.group(1),idx,kind,scope=scope)
            # def blocks push? methods don't contain class scope for nested def decipher; push a placeholder with kind f so 'end' pops, but subsequent defs inside method unlikely.
            stack.append(dict(name=md.group(1),full=(parent['full']+"."+md.group(1) if parent else md.group(1)),kind='f',indent=indent))
            continue
        mconst=re.match(r'^([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)\s*=',s)
        if mconst:
            add(mconst.group(1),idx,'C',scope=scope)
            continue
        # attr_accessor etc kind A ?
        macc=re.match(r'^(attr_accessor|attr_reader|attr_writer)\s+(.+)$',s)
        if macc:
            for sym in re.findall(r':([A-Za-z_][\w]*)',macc.group(2)):
                add(sym,idx,'A',scope=scope)
            continue
    return tags

def parse_perl(state, path, display, lines, lang="Perl"):
    tags=[]
    pkg=None
    for idx,raw in enumerate(lines):
        s=raw.strip()
        if s.startswith("#"): continue
        mp=re.match(r'^package\s+([\w:]+)\s*;',s)
        if mp:
            pkg=mp.group(1)
            t=Tag(pkg,display,idx+1,raw,'p',lang); t.roles="def"; tags.append(t); continue
        ms=re.match(r'^sub\s+([A-Za-z_][\w]*)',s)
        if ms:
            t=Tag(ms.group(1),display,idx+1,raw,'s',lang); t.roles="def"
            if pkg:
                t.scope_kind_letter='p'; t.scope_name=pkg
                # But earlier test sub before package had no scope; sub after package? test.pl sub first then package, sub had no scope. For subs after package, maybe scope? We'll keep but filter? Might cause diff if test expects no scope. Check Perl parser: package scope maybe not s field? Let's not set scope for perl subs (?) Safer: no scope.
                t.scope_kind_letter=None; t.scope_name=None
            tags.append(t); continue
        # constant? use constant NAME => 
        mc=re.search(r'\buse\s+constant\s+([A-Za-z_][\w]*)',s)
        if mc:
            t=Tag(mc.group(1),display,idx+1,raw,'c',lang); t.roles="def"; tags.append(t)

def parse_lua(state, path, display, lines, lang="Lua"):
    tags=[]
    for idx,raw in enumerate(lines):
        s=raw.strip()
        if s.startswith("--"): continue
        m=re.match(r'^(?:local\s+)?function\s+([A-Za-z_][\w\.:]*)',s)
        if m:
            name=m.group(1)
            # For "M.foo" or "Class:method", original tags name maybe full or last? Our tests simple foo/bar
            t=Tag(name,display,idx+1,raw,'f',lang); t.roles="def"; tags.append(t); continue
        m2=re.match(r'^([A-Za-z_][\w\.:]*)\s*=\s*function\b',s)
        if m2:
            t=Tag(m2.group(1),display,idx+1,raw,'f',lang); t.roles="def"; tags.append(t)

def parse_make(state, path, display, lines, lang="Make"):
    tags=[]
    for idx,raw in enumerate(lines):
        if raw.startswith("\t"): continue
        s=raw.strip()
        if s.startswith("#"): continue
        # variable: VAR = , VAR := , VAR += , VAR ?=
        mv=re.match(r'^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*[:+?]?=',raw)
        if mv:
            t=Tag(mv.group(1),display,idx+1,raw,'m',lang); t.roles="def"; tags.append(t); continue
        # target: name: deps (not variable, not %? targets may include .)
        mt=re.match(r'^([A-Za-z0-9_.\-/][^:=]*?)\s*:\s*(?:[^=]|$)',raw)
        if mt and not raw.startswith("."):
            # targets may be multiple space separated before colon
            targets=mt.group(1).strip().split()
            for name in targets:
                if name and not name.startswith("$") and "%" not in name:
                    t=Tag(name,display,idx+1,raw,'t',lang); t.roles="def"; tags.append(t)
            continue
        if mt and raw.startswith("."):
            # .PHONY etc? Probably not tag target? Skip special?
            # Could be ".PHONY: all" deps not targets. skip
            continue
    return tags

def parse_markdown(state, path, display, lines, lang="Markdown"):
    tags=[]
    # chapter = # (level1), section = ##, S = ###? Wait list-kinds Markdown: c chapters, s sections, S level2? Actually earlier list: Markdown kinds printing gave c chapters, s sections, S level 2 sections?? Let's check meta: test md output: Title (#) c, Section1 (##) s scope chapter:Title, Sub (###) S scope section:Title""Section1 (weird quoting due separator "")
    # Kind mapping from test: '#'=c, '##'=s, '###'=S, presumably '####'=t, '#####'=T, '######'=u
    kinds_by_level=['c','s','S','t','T','u']
    stack=[]  # (level,name,kind,full)
    in_fence=False
    for idx,raw in enumerate(lines):
        if raw.strip().startswith("```"):
            in_fence=not in_fence; continue
        if in_fence: continue
        m=re.match(r'^(#{1,6})\s+(.+?)\s*#*\s*$',raw)
        if m:
            level=len(m.group(1)); name=m.group(2).strip()
            kind=kinds_by_level[level-1] if level<=6 else 's'
            while stack and stack[-1][0]>=level:
                stack.pop()
            parent=stack[-1] if stack else None

Implement in format_etags_section: if t.pattern_override is not None: linetext=t.pattern_override

# pseudo semantics: '*' specially is treated as enabling all regardless sign. Maybe '*' is a pseudo-tag name representing wildcard and +/- is part of spec like set operation where * alone expands but - ignored due bug? Observed -* list-pseudo all on, not off. So in apply_pseudo, if body == "*", always add all regardless op. What if --pseudo-tags=-* after + specific? Still all. We'll replicate bug.
# What about disabling all real way? --extras=-p disables pseudo extra completely file.
./executable '--extras=-p' -f /tmp/ps/tags /tmp/ps/a.py && cat /tmp/ps/tags
# options dir diff details re-run single
python3 /tmp/single_diff.py --options=/tmp/p3 -f - /tmp/p3/a.py
# what .ctags files in /tmp/p3? opts.ctags, my.ctags, my2.ctags (contains "--sort=no --fields=+n" which caused Invalid sort in ref? Our options-dir processing loads all *.ctags sorted, maybe ref loads only something else)
ls /tmp/p3/*.ctags; for f in /tmp/p3/*.ctags; do echo "== $f"; cat "$f"; done
./executable --options=/tmp/p3 -f - /tmp/p3/a.py > /tmp/ro.txt 2>/tmp/re.txt; echo rc:$?; cat /tmp/ro.txt; cat /tmp/re.txt
/tmp/newbin/executable --options=/tmp/p3 -f - /tmp/p3/a.py > /tmp/no.txt 2>/tmp/ne.txt; echo rc:$?; cat /tmp/no.txt; cat /tmp/ne.txt

# Anonymous naming hash investigation: __anone62936030108 for /tmp/p3/anon.c line1 struct. 'e62936030' maybe hash of something + '108'? Second 'e62936030203' difference: hash maybe 0xe6293603 and appended byte offset? Offsets: struct at line1 byte 0? 108 ??? Let's gather examples
cat > /tmp/anon1.c <<'EOF'
struct { int a; } v1;
struct { int b; } v2;
union { int c; } v3;
enum { X } v4;
EOF
./executable -f - --sort=no /tmp/anon1.c
cp /tmp/anon1.c /tmp/anon2.c

printf 'struct { int a; } v1;\n' > /tmp/a1.c
printf '\nstruct { int a; } v1;\n' > /tmp/a2.c
./executable -f - --sort=no /tmp/a1.c; ./executable -f - --sort=no /tmp/a2.c

def djb(s):
    h=5381
    for b in s.encode(): h=((h*33)+b)&0xffffffff
    return f"{h:08x}"
for s in ["/tmp/anon1.c","anon1.c","/tmp/p3/anon.c","anon.c","struct","struct { int a; }"]:
    print(s,djb(s))
PY
"}
